F4_baserate_ceiling: (a) Dotted line: best of the four models (random forest 0.860). Uses market identity, the variable this study keeps out of the models. Market recovered for 35% of test rows; every test market also appears in training. (b) No test market appears in training (0%), so the true market's base rate cannot be formed at all. The recovered-market proxy still reaches 0.677 by borrowing the base rates of the training markets a listing most resembles.
F7_feature_ablation: Gradient boosting, loose licence definition, 5 folds per cell; the same fold definitions as the main benchmark. Groups are ordered by panel (a). The gap is the random-split AUC minus the market-hold-out AUC.
F3_learning_curve: Gradient boosting, outcome: loose licence definition. Panel (a): 5 random market draws per point (1 at K=98, the whole pool); band spans the minimum and maximum draw. Evaluation is always the same 150,000 rows from 25 markets withheld from every fit.
F5_two_definitions: Panel (c): markets where the two definitions differ by more than 5 pp (11 of 123). The loose definition counts any non-empty `license` string; the strict one keeps only values that parse as a registration identifier. In Berlin, 29.57% of the values the loose definition adds are DSA trader-information strings, not licences.
F6_calibration_decision_y_license: Gradient boosting, full training fold; outcome: loose licence definition. Shared evaluation subsample, folds pooled. Panel (a): 20 equal-count bins; the diagonal is perfect calibration.
F6_calibration_decision_y_strict: Gradient boosting, full training fold; outcome: strict licence definition. Shared evaluation subsample, folds pooled. Panel (a): 20 equal-count bins; the diagonal is perfect calibration.
F1_validation_design: Outcome: loose licence definition. Panels (a) and (c): mean over folds (5 folds, 1 for the temporal split); bars are ±1 SD across folds. Panel (b): folds pooled into one evaluation set restricted to the 123 markets common to all designs, resampling markets (1,000 draws) so that listings of the same market move together; the pooled market-hold-out estimate (0.740) is slightly below the fold mean in (a) because pooling weights markets by their number of rows. No model receives any market identifier.
